domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into writing the steps, expected results and preconditions as a document, then filing it in the repository.
length_reasoning: A simple procedure for a small feature takes about half an hour to write up; a procedure for a complex or regulated flow with many steps, data setups and traceability takes several hours.
review_reasoning: A reviewer skims a short procedure against the template; a typical one needs steps checked for clarity and completeness; a long regulated one needs the steps walked through and traced to requirements.
stakes_reasoning: An unclear or incomplete procedure usually causes rework or inconsistent test runs, but in regulated products an audit gap is costly.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's templates, product behavior and documentation standards, learned in a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into entering the refund, exchange or adjustment in the billing or order system.
length_reasoning: A simple refund entry within a call takes a couple of minutes; an exchange or multi-line bill adjustment with approvals takes around ten.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the entry portion of the recorded contact and checks the system record against what was promised; longer adjustments take a little more.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong amount or wrong account is usually corrected on complaint, but money has moved and large adjustments are financial loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's remedy rules, limits and billing system, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is typing notes into the ticketing system and updating its fields.
length_reasoning: A routine ticket takes a couple of minutes to document; a long troubleshooting history takes ten to fifteen.
review_reasoning: A lead glances at a short note; a typical note needs the steps and outcome read; a long one needs the sequence followed.
stakes_reasoning: A poor record is noticed when someone later picks up the ticket and costs a little rework.
context_reasoning: Needs the help desk's ticket conventions and category scheme, picked up quickly.

domain_reasoning: The time goes into entering the remedy into billing or order systems and noting the case.
length_reasoning: A straightforward refund from a queued case takes a few minutes; an adjustment needing lookup of history and several entries takes around twenty.
review_reasoning: A supervisor compares the entry to the approved remedy; larger adjustments need the account history checked.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong refund or adjustment is a payment error, partly recoverable but a financial loss.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's systems and remedy policies, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, little else is needed beyond occasionally consulting the case notes on screen, which is the main non-talk activity.
length_reasoning: A simple result callback takes three or four minutes; a contested claim outcome with many questions takes fifteen.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer listens to the recorded call, partly at higher speed, and checks it against the case file.
stakes_reasoning: Misstating a result causes confusion, complaints and callbacks but can be corrected.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's claims process and wording rules, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is writing and revising a standards or criteria document.
length_reasoning: A short checklist of release criteria takes a few hours of drafting; a full quality standard with consultation takes several days of active work.
review_reasoning: Managers read a short criteria list quickly; a typical standard needs each criterion weighed; a full standard needs close reading against practice.
stakes_reasoning: Weak criteria let defective releases through or block good ones, affecting many later releases.
context_reasoning: Needs deep knowledge of the product, release history, risk appetite and team practice, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written diagnosis and recommendation drawn from notes and logs.
length_reasoning: A short summary of a clear issue takes fifteen minutes; a diagnosis with logs, reproduction steps and options takes a couple of hours.
review_reasoning: A reader skims a short note; a typical one needs the reasoning checked against the evidence; a long one needs reproduction or log checks.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong diagnosis sent to a customer or developers causes wasted work or a bad fix but can be reversed.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and the customer's setup, learned over weeks to months.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into running the build or reproducing the steps in the application and updating the tracker, which is operating software rather than writing code.
length_reasoning: A simple fix is re-checked in ten minutes; a fix needing environment setup, regression checks or data takes over an hour.
review_reasoning: A colleague reads the note and repeats the check; for complex fixes the regression checks must also be repeated.
stakes_reasoning: A fix wrongly closed usually resurfaces in testing or from users, with rework.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's behavior, environments and defect conventions, learned over weeks.

unit_flag_reason: A curation pass covers many records of mixed kinds (merging, status updates, workarounds), so it mixes very different amounts and types of work.
domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into working through records in the defect-tracking database, merging and editing them.
length_reasoning: A light pass before a minor milestone takes under an hour; a full pass over a large backlog takes most of a day.
review_reasoning: A reviewer spot-checks merges and statuses; a large pass needs a sample of merges and workarounds checked against the originals.
stakes_reasoning: Wrong merges or workarounds mislead support and developers but can be reversed.
context_reasoning: Judging duplicates and valid workarounds needs deep familiarity with the product's defect history, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written answer, mostly composed from the question and knowledge-base or manual lookups.
length_reasoning: A familiar question is answered in a few minutes; an unusual one needing research and a step-by-step reply takes around half an hour.
review_reasoning: A lead skims a short answer; a typical one needs the steps checked for correctness; a long one needs verification against documentation.
stakes_reasoning: Wrong instructions reach the user and cause a follow-up, but are reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's standard setups and software, learned over a few weeks.

unit_flag_reason: The item spans quick fixes and long diagnostic investigations that include escalation, so it mixes very different kinds of work.
domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into operating diagnostic tools, admin consoles and the user's system.
length_reasoning: Many tickets are resolved in a quarter of an hour; hard ones take a couple of hours of active work.
review_reasoning: A lead reads the notes of a quick fix; a typical one needs the cause and fix checked; a long one needs the diagnostic chain followed.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong fix usually shows up as a recurring problem and is corrected, though lost data or downtime is possible.
context_reasoning: Needs the organization's systems, configurations and history, built over months.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into writing scripts, plans and briefings and emailing participants, which is document and message work.
length_reasoning: A small round with an existing script takes a few hours of organizing; a larger third-party round with new scripts and access setup takes several days.
review_reasoning: A manager reads the plan and scripts; larger rounds need access, schedule and scripts checked item by item.
stakes_reasoning: A badly organized round wastes participants' time and delays findings but is recoverable; external parties may see the product.
context_reasoning: Needs the product, environments and the people involved, learned over weeks to months.

domain_reasoning: Most of the time goes into operating the test tool and the application and entering results in the test management tool.
length_reasoning: A short automated run is triggered and logged in minutes; a manual session of many cases takes hours.
review_reasoning: A lead glances at logged pass results; a typical run needs failures checked; a long manual session needs a sample of cases verified.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly recorded result can hide a defect, which is usually caught later in testing.
context_reasoning: Needs the test environment, tools and product behavior, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is entering case details into the referral or ticketing system and attaching history.
length_reasoning: A simple referral takes five minutes; a complex grievance with a long history takes around thirty.
review_reasoning: The receiving department reads the referral for completeness; complex ones need the history checked.
stakes_reasoning: A poor referral delays resolution and annoys the customer, but is fixed by asking for more detail.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's department structure and routing rules, learned over a few weeks.

unit_flag_reason: A day's log aggregates many entries of different kinds over a whole shift, so it is a collection of many small writing tasks rather than one deliverable.
domain_reasoning: The log is built from entries typed into a logging system or ticket tool during the day.
length_reasoning: Active logging time across a day is small, perhaps half an hour to an hour and a half.
review_reasoning: A supervisor skims the day's log; auditors check a sample against tickets and installation records.
stakes_reasoning: Gaps in logs are usually minor but can matter in audits.
context_reasoning: Needs the organization's logging conventions and systems, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking up the policy in the system and noting the account.
length_reasoning: A clear coverage question takes about five minutes; one needing careful reading of policy terms takes fifteen.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the call and checks the answer against the policy wording and note.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong coverage answer can mislead a customer into false expectations or to forgo a claim, causing complaints or liability.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the insurer's policy forms and coverage rules, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written evaluation and recommendation based on specifications, trial notes and comparison.
length_reasoning: A small evaluation takes a few hours of active work; a major upgrade or product comparison takes several days.
review_reasoning: A manager reads a short evaluation; larger ones need claims, costs and test results checked.
stakes_reasoning: A poor recommendation can lead to a costly or hard-to-reverse purchase.
context_reasoning: Needs the organization's infrastructure, needs and budgets, built over months.
